messages:
matt: OK team — need to lock H1/H2 capacity scenarios and a recommendation for enterprise onramp by EOD Fri. Customers expect predictable latency and commit pricing. Please vote and call out blockers.
jess: +1. do we have updated lead times from vendors? that'll change commit sizing.
omar: vendor TLs: H100 12-16w, A800 8-12w, some spot availability for A100 in 4-6w. those are best-case.
li: unrolled three scenarios in the doc (quick sketch):

```
Scenario A: conservative commit
  - reserve 60% of forecasted peak
  - regions: EU + NA first, APAC 6mo lag
  - target fleet util: 65%-70%
Scenario B: hybrid commit + spot
  - reserve 35%, use spot/backfill for bursts
  - regions: EU + NA simultaneous, APAC soft-launch
  - target util: 75%-80%
Scenario C: aggressive commit (enterprise-first)
  - reserve 85% for enterprise tier; fewer spots
  - regions: prioritize customers' target regions
  - target util: 60%-70% (higher cost)
```

li: numbers are very rough; assumes average seq len 128 for prod workloads.
sara: for SLA and canary rollouts we should require a 2-week canary in EU and NA before APAC turnup. any scenario that skips that increases risk.
karen: cost-wise scenario B saves ~18% vs C on unit token cost in our sim, but adds complexity to ops.
ryan: ops risks for B: spot evictions during large generative workloads. we need fallback model variants and routing policy ready.
matt: key customer asks: 1) guaranteed throughput for enterprise pilot (not necessarily full commit), 2) regional isolation in EU, 3) audit logs and KMS for private deploys.
jess: vote: A = 0, B = +1 (preferred), C = 0 for me. B balances cost and customer risk with extra work.
omar: vote B as well. we can improve fallback by pre-warming cheaper quantized variants.
li: question for infra-sre: if we go B and hit sustained eviction events, are we comfortable auto-scaling catch-up capacity in NA to protect enterprise SLAs?
ops-bot: @matt FYI: autoscaler policy 'burst-protect-v2' current headroom = 12% (can be raised, may increase spend).
ryan: we can raise headroom to 25% for enterprise rollouts but need finance signoff for burn window.
sara: can product commit to a cutoff of non-critical workloads in the 4-week launch window to reduce eviction surface? we need a launch gating checklist.
matt: yes — product pledge: deprioritize batch embeddings for two weeks post-launch for pilot customers.
karen: finance note: increasing headroom to 25% adds ~$120k/month. need PO by next Wed to lock vendor pricing.
jess: Ops actionables if we pick B:
- prepare fallback routing (quantized variant) + test failover path
- run eviction chaos test on staging (simulate 30% spot loss)
- update autoscaler policy and get finance approval
li: infra actionables:
- draft commit SLOs: what % of capacity guaranteed per customer tier
- region cadence plan (EU + NA Q1 turnup, APAC soft Q3)
matt: decision: seems like B has majority. I'll run a quick sync with finance and product in 1hr. if no major objections we adopt B and start vendor negotiations for a 35% reserved commit across EU/NA.
ryan: noted. I'll prepare a short cost/impact slide for finance and list tradeoffs.
omar: I'll scope the quantized variant rollout and testing plan.
sara: tagging @karen for PO timeline and @li for commit SLO draft.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: `infra/procurement/commit-plan#v1` -> awaiting approval.
matt: final note — if vendor lead-times slip >4w from current estimate we need to revisit and consider moving to more aggressive commit earlier. call out any red flags asap.
karen: PO timeline OK if decision by Tue EOD; otherwise pricing may change.
li: will post the SLO draft and the scenario spreadsheet in #eng-infra after this thread.
jess: thanks all — B seems like the pragmatic choice. :thumbsup:
matt: thanks — action owners: @li SLOs, @omar fallbacks, @ryan finance slide, @karen PO. I'll follow up after the 1hr sync.
